classification.difficultyReason: Infer radii from three semicircular arc lengths, then subtract two smaller semicircle areas from the larger semicircle area.

content.prompt: The arc lengths of three semicircles are given. Find the area of the shaded region.

spec.description: A large semicircle contains two equal smaller semicircles on the same baseline. Their adjacent diameters partition its diameter. The large curved arc is labelled 12π cm and each smaller curved arc is labelled 6π cm. Only the region inside the large semicircle and outside both smaller semicircles has light purple fill. Ordinary outlines and labels use house black.
spec.mathematics: The large radius is twice each smaller radius. All three measurements label curved arc lengths, excluding the straight diameters.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the requested shaded region are visible; radii and calculated areas are not supplied.

answer.short:
$36\pi\ \mathrm{cm}^2$

Find each radius from its semicircular arc length, then subtract the two smaller semicircle areas.
answer.worked:
A semicircular arc has length $\pi r$. Let $R$ be the large radius and $r$ each smaller radius.

$$\begin{align*}\pi R&=12\pi\\R&=12\ \mathrm{cm}\\\pi r&=6\pi\\r&=6\ \mathrm{cm}\end{align*}$$

Subtract the two smaller semicircle areas from the larger semicircle area.

$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{shaded}}&=\frac12\pi(12)^2-2\left(\frac12\pi(6)^2\right)\\A_{\text{shaded}}&=72\pi-36\pi\\A_{\text{shaded}}&=36\pi\ \mathrm{cm}^2\end{align*}$$
